images.alt: Paulus schrijft met tranen — 2 Korinthiërs 2:4; tekstillustratie.
images.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Photorealistic illustration of an explicit biblical comparison or event, first-century Roman Judea and Galilee, landscape 3:2, natural materials and daylight, anatomically coherent people with exactly two arms and animals with correct limbs; fully covering modest opaque robes. No modern objects, readable writing, portrait of God the Father, blood, injury or watermark. 2 Corinthians 2:4 says Paul wrote in sorrow, anguish and many tears to show his love. A first-century adult Paul sits alone at a simple wooden table with a papyrus letter and reed pen, eyes visibly moist and face saddened yet compassionate. No extreme despair or self-harm, no readable writing, no modern paper or fountain pen. Coherent two arms, one hand resting by the letter and one gently touching his cheek. Soft lamplight, modest fully covering robes. The scene illustrates the stated sorrow of the letter, no invented recipient present.

images.alt: Paulus neemt afscheid in Troas — 2 Korinthiërs 2:13; tekstillustratie.
images.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Photorealistic illustration of an explicit biblical comparison or event, first-century Roman Judea and Galilee, landscape 3:2, natural materials and daylight, anatomically coherent people with exactly two arms and animals with correct limbs; fully covering modest opaque robes. No modern objects, readable writing, portrait of God the Father, blood, injury or watermark. 2 Corinthians 2:12–13: Paul finds an open opportunity in Troas but has no rest because Titus is absent, so he takes leave and goes toward Macedonia. Show Paul with a small travel bag saying farewell to two adult believers beside a modest ancient Aegean harbour. Three main adults, Titus explicitly absent. A wooden first-century merchant vessel rests in the distant harbour, no later stone castle or modern ship. Expressions of concern and warm farewell, no invented reunion with Titus.

images.scene: Mozes legt een doek over zijn gezicht
images.alt: Mozes legt een doek over zijn gezicht — 2 Korinthiërs 3:13; tekstillustratie.
images.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Photorealistic illustration of an explicit biblical comparison or event, first-century Roman Judea and Galilee, landscape 3:2, natural materials and daylight, anatomically coherent people with exactly two arms and animals with correct limbs; fully covering modest opaque robes. No modern objects, readable writing, portrait of God the Father, blood, injury or watermark. 2 Corinthians 3:7 and 13 recalls Moses with a veil over his face. Clearly ancient Mosaic-era wilderness camp, NOT first-century Roman Judea: elderly bearded Moses in modest opaque robes lifts a plain linen veil over his radiant face while two Israelites in simple ancient desert clothing stand a little distance away. The fabric covers his face; soft bright light behind the veil, no portrait of God, no extra hands, no horns, no elaborate crown or readable stone tablets. Exactly three adults, dignified and nonviolent. This is the earlier biblical episode quoted by Paul, not a contemporary event in Corinth.
